articles.title: WSL roundup: Putellas scores first London City goal, Greenwood keeps Manchester City perfect
articles.summary: Two-time Ballon d’Or winner nets against Brighton. Alex Greenwood’s City free-kick sinks Charlton. Alexia Putellas scored her first WSL goal as London City Lionesses moved second in the table after beating Brighton 2-0 at home.
body: The two-time Ballon d’Or winner, who left Barcelona in the summer, put her side ahead in the 29th minute when she slotted a low shot into the far corner.

Brighton were close to an equaliser before the break when Emily Murphy’s header struck the crossbar. The hosts then made sure of the points in stoppage time as Lucía Corrales slotted home a cross from Delphine Cascarino.
Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the Women’s Super League season with a 1-0 win at Charlton.
Alex Greenwood scored a fine free-kick in the 36th minute, which proved enough to give the defending champions a fourth successive WSL victory.

articles.title: 'Mr Saturday' Russell 'comes through other side after real tough period'
articles.summary: George Russell described the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as "the most dominant weekend I've had in my career" after a win that felt like vindication.
body: For George Russell, this one felt like vindication, proof that he had "come through the other side" and was back to his best after what he acknowledged was a "real tough period" during this Formula 1 season.
The Mercedes driver's victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, holding off Red Bull's Max Verstappen in one of the closest finishes in history, was his first since the end of June - seven races ago.
In that time, team-mate Kimi Antonelli has won three times, to take his tally of victories to eight for the season.

So Russell needed this, his third victory, in a year that he started as championship favourite. Instead, Antonelli has taken the season by the throat and all but crushed the life out of Russell's hopes.

articles.title: Trump flyover and Secret Service checks greet fans at marquee Texas v Tennessee clash
articles.summary: Air Force One flies low over Neyland before kickoff. Schools coordinate with Secret Service over headsets. Fans urged to arrive early amid enhanced screening. Encouraging fans to get inside Neyland Stadium earlier than usual with Donald Trump coming to Tennessee’s college football game against…
body: Security checks on the stadium’s perimeter went relatively smoothly with Tennessee officials opening the stadium 30 minutes earlier than normal. Fans got half-price off concessions as a reward for showing up early, and Tennessee faithful had the stands half full 90 minutes before kickoff and nearly packed an hour before.

Those in their seats were treated to a low-altitude flyover by Air Force One as the US president came into town with the Volunteers and Longhorns warming up on the field below. Trump landed at 11.28am ET ahead of the noon kickoff, according to reporters traveling with the president.

Trump’s motorcade arrived at Neyland Stadium just as the national anthem was being sung at 11.59am. Trump pumped his first a couple times when shown in his seat on the videoboards with Tennessee’s US senators on either side. One of them, Marsha Blackburn, is running for governor of Tennessee.
The president’s visit won’t affect communications between coaches and players on the field thanks to some coordination before Saturday’s game.

articles.title: Wallaroos storm back in second half to blow away Scotland in WXV series
articles.summary: Scotland 10-30 Australia. Visitors trail 10-5 in Edinburgh but battle back. The Wallaroos delivered the most accomplished display of their European campaign, roaring back from a half-time deficit to blow away Scotland 30-10 and end a six-match losing streak.
body: After two tough defeats to world champions England and fellow powerhouse outfit France in successive weekends, the Wallaroos marked Michaela Leonard’s historic 50th Test with a second-half display of power and precision in Edinburgh.

Down 10-5 at the break, Australia, who hadn’t won a Test all season, conjured up their best form, scoring three well-worked tries in the space of just eight minutes and going on to rack up 25 unanswered points to dominate their WXV Global Series clash at Hive Stadium, next door to Murrayfield.

It proved a landmark day for two standouts, with the 31-year-old lock Leonard becoming the first Wallaroo ever to win a half-century of caps and Desiree Miller scoring their opening try six minutes before the break to rack up 100 Test points.

The 24-year-old Sydney speedster’s try still wasn’t enough to drag Australia back on to level terms as the No 8 Evie Gallagher’s 15th minute score, plus a conversion and penalty from Helen Nelson, gave the hosts the interval advantage. The Wallaroos’ post-break resurgence was then stimulated by the captain, Siokapesi Palu, and an inspiring rallying cry to her team at half-time.

articles.title: Bairstow six seals one-wicket win for Yorkshire
articles.summary: Captain Jonny Bairstow hits the winning runs as Yorkshire beat Nottinghamshire by one wicket in their final Championship match of the season.
body: Yorkshire ended their County Championship season with a third consecutive victory after beating Nottinghamshire by one wicket on day three at Trent Bridge.
Needing just 158 to win with more than five sessions left in the match, they suffered a major wobble in which seven wickets fell for 61 runs.
It followed an earlier collapse by Nottinghamshire in their second innings as they crashed from 55-3 overnight to 85 all out, losing seven wickets for 30 runs in the space of 17.1 overs.
Jack White took four of those to finish with a season's best 5-23, Ben Coad picking up the others for figures of 4-27.

articles.title: Kent celebrate promotion by beating Gloucestershire
articles.summary: Kent complete victory against Gloucestershire, with their promotion to Division One having already been confirmed by Northamptonshire's earlier defeat.
body: Kent celebrated promotion to Division One of the County Championship with an eight-wicket win over Gloucestershire at Canterbury.
Matt Milnes took 5-33 as Gloucestershire were dismissed for 241, despite a battling 66 from. Kamran Dhariwal.
And by the time Kent started the chase they already knew they'd been promoted, after learning their only rivals, Northamptonshire had lost to Middlesex at Lord's.
Sam Northeast then hit an unbeaten 49 and England's Zak Crawley made 44, as the home side cruised home, finishing on 120-2.

articles.title: Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal Made 2017 Bigger but Is The 2026 Laver Cup Actually Stronger?
articles.summary: Put the first Laver Cup roster next to the current one and there is an obvious winner in one category. Name value. The inaugural 2017 edition had Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer on the same team, with a 20-year-old Alexander Zverev, Marin Cilic, Dominic Thiem and Tomas Berdych beside them.
body: That is difficult to compete with. But name value and playing strength are not necessarily the same thing. If we ignore what those players eventually achieved and instead compare how highly they were actually ranked when each Laver Cup took place, the 2026 field holds up remarkably well.

Rafael Nadal No. 1, Roger Federer No. 2, Alexander Zverev No. 4, Marin Cilic No. 5, Dominic Thiem No. 7 and Tomas Berdych No. 19. That is absurdly strong. Five of the six were inside the Top ten, while Berdych was hardly some weak final selection at No. 19. Europe had an average ranking of No. 6.3.

Team World was considerably weaker on paper. Sam Querrey was No. 16, John Isner No. 17, Nick Kyrgios No. 20, Jack Sock No. 21, Denis Shapovalov No. 51 and Frances Tiafoe No. 72. Tiafoe had entered late after Juan Martin del Potro withdrew. The average Team World ranking was therefore No. 32.8. That tells you almost everything about the first Laver Cup.
Europe was ridiculous. World was entertaining. The overall field was not nearly as balanced as memory sometimes makes it seem.
points: Put the first Laver Cup roster next to the current one and there is an obvious winner in one category.
The inaugural 2017 edition had Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer on the same team, with a 20-year-old Alexander Zverev, Marin Cilic, Dominic Thiem and Tomas Berdych beside them.
If we ignore what those players eventually achieved and instead compare how highly they were actually ranked when each Laver Cup took place, the 2026 field holds up remarkably well.
Rafael Nadal No. 1, Roger Federer No. 2, Alexander Zverev No. 4, Marin Cilic No. 5, Dominic Thiem No. 7 and Tomas Berdych No. 19.

articles.title: Texas football: Colin Simmons flagged after simulating a bathroom break after sack
articles.summary: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. - During the second quarter Saturday at Tennessee, star Texas football edge rusher Colin Simmons made a big play. And then he got called for a bigger penalty.
body: Simmons was flagged for an unsportsmanlike conduct after celebrating a third-down sack of Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon. While explaining the penalty at Neyland Stadium, referee Kyle Olson explained that Simmons simulated using the restroom during his celebration.

That 15-yard penalty turned a fourth-and-29 play at the Tennessee 12-yard line into a first down. Simmons, though, dodged a bullet as Tennessee eventually reached Texas territory before failing on a fourth-down attempt.
Over the first two quarters of Saturday's game, Simmons recorded five tackles and two sacks.

Despite being penalized eight times for 75 yards in the first half, Texas still entered halftime with a 10-3 lead. Two of those penalties were called on UT quarterback Arch Manning, who was twice guilty of throwing the football beyond the line of scrimmage.

articles.title: Putellas' first WSL goal helps send London City second with Brighton win
articles.summary: Alexia Putellas scored her first goal in English football, helping London City Lionesses to a 2-0 win against Brighton and sending them second in the WSL table.
body: London City Lionesses vs Brighton and Hove Albion Women. Barclays Women's Super League.

The biggest signing of the summer collected a rebounded save after Chiamaka Nnadozie initially stopped Kadidiatou Diani's strike. She then swerved a half-volley around her defender that beat the still-recovering goalkeeper.

It was the first real chance of a first half that lacked many, although Brighton almost equalised instantly. Emily Murphy's header curled onto the crossbar though and Keiko Seike - who was impressive defensively - could not sort her feet out to slot home the loose ball.

Lucia Corrales rounded off the victory late on, finishing a wonderful team break. Danielle van de Donk stole the ball away from Fran Kirby, releasing Delphine Cascarino, who in turn picked out the incoming run of Corrales on the left, who emphatically finished.

articles.title: Roma competing with Hull City for Frosinone’s Giorgio Kvernadze
articles.summary: Frosinone have caught many by surprise in the Serie A this season, as they find themselves inside the top six. Attacker Giorgi Kvernadze has caught specific attention, having found the net three times already in the season.
body: Corriere dello Sport report that Roma were desperate for another attacking signing in the summer. They pursued moves for several players for that role but nothing really materialised.

They are expected to push for a player in that position once again in the summer and Frosinone’s Kvernardze is attracting specific attention. He is believed to be a fit for Gian Piero Gasperini’s system, with the player valued at atleast over €20 million, having joined Frosinone for just around €1 million.

Roma are evaluating a move and have done exploratory research about the player too. Apart from Kvernadze’s ability, he is also seen as someone who is sustainable as a target and offers quite a bit of room for growth.
Hull City have also enquired about the attacker and Roma are hoping his value doesn’t escalate further. It will only help in executing a favourable January move.

articles.title: Juventus is watching AS Monaco star after his failed move to Everton
articles.summary: Juventus remain on the market for at least one new attacker despite the arrivals of Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani during the summer. Both attackers joined after the club lost Lois Openda, Dusan Vlahovic and Jonathan David, meaning the Bianconeri could still benefit from adding another…
body: One player on their radar ahead of the January window is Folarin Balogun, who came close to joining Everton during the last transfer window. The striker decided against the move just hours before the window closed, leaving him at AS Monaco.

Monaco still want to sell Balogun, and his situation has attracted Juventus’ attention. The Bianconeri could now consider making an approach when the transfer window opens, depending on how the situation develops.
Balogun could provide Juventus with another attacking option, while his availability could make him an attractive target for a club looking to strengthen its forward line.

Tuttomercatoweb claims Juventus are among the clubs considering a move for Balogun when the January transfer window opens. The Bianconeri reportedly view him as one of the top players available and could explore the possibility of adding him to their squad.

articles.title: Maracana pitch still being worked on with NFL match just hours away
articles.summary: Workers were still trimming the turf at Maracana Stadium on Saturday, less than 30 hours before the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens.
body: The Maracana's pitch has been a concern for almost two weeks due to its poor shape amid a long season in Brazilian football, with Rio clubs Flamengo and Fluminense playing there at least once a week.
Maracana workers were using mows and scissors big and small to perfect the turf for the game, in an effort expected to end just hours before kick-off.

On Friday, the executive director of the NFL Players Association said both the NFL and the players union have had experts monitoring the field conditions for Sunday's game. The union's experts are worried about loose turf leading to too much slipping.
Concerns are about the turf's traction and stability, which made the NFL reinforce its stitching. Earlier this week, field director Nick Pappas said he was confident players will have no trouble.

articles.title: What did Pocognoli change in first Scotland game in charge?
articles.summary: A draw might not be the most inspiring result for a new era, but there were still plenty of positives for Sebastien Pocognoli to take from his first game in charge of Scotland.
body: On the surface, 0-0 against Slovenia doesn't exactly scream entertaining. On another day though, Scotland could've either won by four or lost by a couple; such was the nature of the contest.
In the first half they looked vulnerable, but the second completely dominant. So, what exactly did Pocognoli do to change things up for the better, and what does he still need to keep his eye on?
Despite his record of qualifying for more major tournaments than any other manager, the one criticism Steve Clarke repeatedly received during his tenure was that Scotland sat too deep.
Pre-match, Pocognoli made a point of emphasising that his ideology was the opposite. "I try to be a little bit higher up the pitch," he said.
